# Chicago Heater Repair Checklist

A tenant in Chicago with no working heat in winter should document the problem carefully, notify the landlord in writing, and keep a clear paper trail. The goal is to create evidence, give the landlord a fair chance to fix it, and prepare a formal demand if the repair is delayed.

## Step-by-Step Tenant Action Plan

| Step | What to do | What to keep |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Record the date, time, indoor temperature, and room affected each day | A simple log with photos of the thermostat and a thermometer |
| 2 | Photograph or video the broken heater and any visible issues | Dated media showing the problem and cold conditions |
| 3 | Save every message with the landlord or property manager | Emails, texts, voicemail notes, and call logs |
| 4 | Send a written repair request if you have not already | A dated email or letter asking for immediate repair |
| 5 | Set a clear deadline for action | A reasonable repair deadline in writing |
| 6 | Escalate if the landlord does not respond | Local tenant hotline, code enforcement, or legal aid contact notes |

## Practical Documentation Checklist

- Write down the exact date you first reported the broken heater: **2025-11-18**
- Note that the apartment temperature has stayed below **18°C** for several days
- Take at least 2 photos per day showing:
  - the thermostat reading
  - a separate thermometer reading, if available
  - the heater itself
- Save screenshots of all texts and emails
- Keep a short incident log with:
  - date
  - time
  - temperature
  - room
  - who you contacted
  - response received
- If you buy space heaters, blankets, or hotel stays, keep receipts
- Do not rely on phone calls alone; follow up in writing after every call

## Formal Written Request Checklist

Use a firm, neutral tone and include these points:

- Your name and unit address
- Lease start date: **2025-08-01**
- Date the problem was reported: **2025-11-18**
- Short description of the issue: broken heater, indoor temperature below 18°C
- Request for immediate repair
- A clear repair deadline
- A request for written confirmation of the repair schedule
- A statement that you are keeping records of the issue and all communications

## Sample Email to the Landlord

**Subject:** Urgent Heat Repair Request for [Your Address]

Dear [Landlord/Property Manager Name],

I am writing to follow up on the broken heater in my apartment at [address]. I first reported this issue on 2025-11-18, and the problem has not been fixed. The indoor temperature has remained below 18°C for several days, which is making the apartment unsafe and unlivable.

Please arrange for the heater to be repaired immediately and confirm in writing when the repair will be completed. If a technician needs access to the unit, I am available at reasonable times and can coordinate access promptly.

For clarity, I have kept records of the temperature, the condition of the heater, and my prior communications about this issue. I would appreciate your written response as soon as possible.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,
[Your Name]
[Unit Number]
[Phone Number]
[Email Address]

## Quick Actions

Action: [Button: Draft letter] https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/demand_letter

- Cornell Legal Information Institute, demand letter basics: https://www.law.cornell.edu/wex/demand_letter
